facts.value: Bachelor of Engineering in Design and Manufacturing Engineering
This BE in Design and Manufacture course prepares graduates to design products from concept through manufacture, real-world use, and end-of-life recycling.
A wide range of employers are seeking graduates with these skills, and the skills are highly transferable across many industry sectors from biomedical devices to Tesla cars to agricultural products.
Industrial Machinery Manufacturing, Medical Equipment Manufacturing, Design Services and Pharmaceutical Manufacturing.
Stryker, Boston Scientific, Regeneron, Johnson & Johnson Vision & Modular Automation.
This course is accredited by Engineers Ireland.
Students graduating from this degree can undertake the MEng in Mechatronics or many other masters programmes in other disciplines at UL.
There are also lots of research opportunities to masters or doctorate level available in the areas of Design and Manufacture.

Cian Hogan.description: Chose Design and Manufacture Engineering for a mix of technical drawing and problem-solving skills. Gained practical knowledge about current practices and equipment used in the manufacturing industry.
Cian Hogan.co_op_experience: Completed 8-month Co-op Placement in Modular Automation in Shannon, Co. Clare, designing custom equipment and gaining industry experience.

Lisa Daly.description: Chose Design and Manufacture Engineering to learn about product innovation and sustainable manufacturing. Gained project management skills and applied theoretical knowledge during her Co-op with Abbott Diagnostics.
Lisa Daly.co_op_experience: Co-op with Abbott Diagnostics helped her understand manufacturing businesses.
Lisa Daly.current_job: Various roles in Abbott's global rotational program including project engineer, operations supervisor, and procurement specialist.
